clue.text: Get a clear picture of bent coppers

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so several coppers are CUs

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get the real story about corrupt police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges OF plus CUS, the plural of Cu, the chemical symbol for copper. 'Bent coppers' reads as British slang for corrupt police.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a lens or the eye to sharpness is to make an image distinct.

clue.text: Pay up in fear for Donnybrook

indicators.note: in places the turned-round payment inside the word for fear

parts.note: fright is sudden fear

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Someone settles a debt out of fear of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FEE to EEF, placed 'in' FRIGHT. Donnybrook, from a rowdy Dublin fair, means a riotous fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Donnybrook is a free-for-all brawl, a fight that anyone may join.

clue.text: Pull a punch

explanation.definitionFit: Clout is influence, as in having pull; it is also a heavy blow with the hand.

clue.text: The rest they use indiscriminately

indicators.note: indiscriminately means randomly, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: The remaining people make use of something without picking or choosing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indiscriminately' rearranges THEY USE. 'The rest' looks like 'the others' but means sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for sleep, a period of repose.

clue.text: Squad nick crazy type in inescapable trap

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A police squad catches some deranged character and holds them in a trap they cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges the nine letters of SQUAD NICK; 'nick' is British slang for arrest. 'type in' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterlogged sand sucks down anything that steps on it, a natural snare that holds its victim.

clue.text: Fruit for Peter, the carpenter

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Quince is the carpenter among the amateur actors in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit; Peter Quince is Shakespeare's carpenter in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Not knowing the answer, I give round number

indicators.note: round says the word for give goes around the abbreviation for number

parts.note: to grant is to give

explanation.surface: Stumped by a question, I hand over a round figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts GRANT around NO; 'round number' looks like a whole figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uninformed means lacking knowledge, here of a reply.

clue.text: Overacts in the bosom of the family — see a lot of hot air

indicators.note: in the bosom of means held inside, so the word for overacts goes within the word for family

parts.note: kin are one's family
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: A relative overdoes it at home, full of bluster and big talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the bosom of' puts HAMS inside KIN. 'hot air' looks like empty talk but is a literal hot wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The khamsin is a hot, dry, dusty wind blowing across Egypt and the Sahara.

clue.text: Conduct business with Bill at its head

indicators.note: at its head means the first piece comes before the second, at the top in a down answer

parts.note: ac is an abbreviation for account, a bill
a company is a business

explanation.surface: A firm runs its affairs with a man named Bill as its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name but is AC, short for account.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany is to escort, as a guide conducts visitors.

clue.text: Put a poster up, showing the timing of events

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to set is to put or place
an ad, an advertisement, can be a poster

explanation.surface: Someone pins a notice on the wall listing when things happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SET + AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates are the days on which things are scheduled to happen.

clue.text: Movement of troops results from change of government, deposing leader

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes the head, so the first letter of the word comes off

parts.note: a revolution is an overthrow and change of government

explanation.surface: Military manoeuvres follow from a coup that removed the country's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing leader' takes the first letter, R, off REVOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: In military usage an evolution is a drill manoeuvre in which a formation changes position.

clue.text: Meeting a Northerner

parts.note: a Scot comes from Scotland, the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Someone is introduced to a person from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse, and a race 'meeting' is a day of horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse whose race days, especially Royal Ascot, are known as a race meeting.

clue.text: March the first not precisely when a legendary character appears

indicators.note: not precisely means inexactly, so the letters of the phrase are put in a different order

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the clock struck'

explanation.surface: The first of March is roughly when a figure from legend shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not precisely' rearranges MARCH THE FIRST into FATHERCHRISTM, and AS ('when') completes it. Of course he really appears in December.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded gift-bringer of Christmas Eve is a figure of folklore and myth.

clue.text: Floor of small stones

explanation.definitionFit: To gravel someone is to baffle or perplex them, as does floor; it is also a loose mass of pebbles.

clue.text: About time to adjust an instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for adjust goes round the word time

parts.note: to alter is to adjust

explanation.surface: It is high time somebody recalibrated a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as 'high time', but 'About' puts ALTER around TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is a gauge in an aircraft that measures height above sea level.

clue.text: Overwhelm one sister one of 8.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun is a religious sister
the answer to 8 Down is a plural, so one of them is the singular

explanation.surface: A nun is overwhelmed, one sister among eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of 8' refers to the answer to 8 Down: one of those is DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood something is to swamp it, as with too much work.

clue.text: Doctor wearing senseless (without going to extremes) outfits

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the trimmed word is put around the doctor
not going to the extremes means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in absurd clothes, though not wildly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without going to extremes' trims senseless to ENSELES; 'wearing' puts it around MB.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a set of matching clothes worn together.

clue.text: Silver and green I mixed and matched

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blends silver and green paint to get a good colour match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges GREEN I into REEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree correspond with each other, as colours that go together.

clue.text: Instruction reversing, for instance, a way to escape losing nothing

indicators.note: reversing tells the solver to read the whole string of pieces backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example', for instance

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the zero leaves the word

parts.note: a let-out is a loophole or way to escape
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lesson on reversing out of trouble, say, when you have nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes O out of LETOUT to leave LETUT; EG + A + LETUT is read backwards by 'reversing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guardianship and the teaching that a tutor gives a pupil.

clue.text: German rock and roll arranged to incorporate note that's coming up

indicators.note: to incorporate means to take within, so the musical note goes inside the jumble
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the word before it are reordered

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A German rock and roll band's arrangement includes a note that is approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns ROLL into LORL, which incorporates E; 'coming up' reverses IE. The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a steep slate cliff on the Rhine, home in legend of a siren.

clue.text: Girl's jewels

explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a female name, and beryls are precious gemstones such as emerald and aquamarine.

clue.text: Keeping calm as river rises outside

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the reversed river goes around the Latin word
in a down clue rises means read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Elbe is a river of central Europe
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Staying composed while the river level climbs outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses ELBE to EBLE, placed 'outside' QUA.
explanation.definitionFit: An even-tempered person is equable, not easily upset.

clue.text: Foul — silly after I became objective

indicators.note: the subject pronoun I in its objective form becomes me

explanation.surface: Something ridiculous gets nasty after I turn to cold facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I became objective' replaces I in silly with ME, its objective case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul stinks, giving off a bad odour.

clue.text: Writer, Wells's setting a disgusted expression in the middle of address to lady

parts.note: the cathedral city of Wells is in Somerset, a county in south-west England

indicators.note: in the middle of says the exclamation sits within the form of address

parts.note: ma'am is the polite way to address a lady
ugh is a cry of disgust

explanation.surface: H. G. Wells writes a scene in which he greets a lady with obvious distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like the novelist H. G. Wells but is the city in Somerset. 'in the middle of' puts UGH inside MAAM.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Somerset Maugham was an English novelist, playwright and short-story author.

clue.text: Child in charge of sound

parts.note: a son is a child

explanation.surface: A boy is put in control of the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective for sound waves and audible vibration.

clue.text: Run into — cut up rough

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the word for chopped

parts.note: to hash is to chop up
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone crashes into a person who then gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' goes 'into' HASH; 'cut up rough' is British for getting angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh means severe and coarse, as rough treatment is.

clue.text: You'll find nothing as trustworthy as lithography in the early stages of reproduction

indicators.note: the early stages of each word are its opening letters, so these five words give their first letters

explanation.surface: Nothing is as reliable as lithography at the start of printing copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' suggests printing copies, as lithography does, but here it means giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, the moment when an offspring is born.

clue.text: William I backed by uncouth earl lacking culture

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the name and the letter are read in reverse

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William

indicators.note: uncouth means rough and disorderly, so the letters of the title are scrambled

explanation.surface: William the Conqueror has the support of a coarse nobleman with no refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses BILL + I to ILLIB; 'uncouth' rearranges EARL into ERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal in its older sense means without a liberal education, unrefined and narrow-minded.

clue.text: What anglers may be after, lying appallingly, with a lot of nit-picking

parts.note: carp are freshwater fish that anglers try to catch

indicators.note: appallingly means dreadfully, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishermen telling dreadful lies while finding fault with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appallingly' rearranges LYING into INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping means making petty complaints, so doing it in this manner is fault-finding.

clue.text: Characteristics of people some of whom get hospitalized.

indicators.note: some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run hidden within it

explanation.surface: A trait shared by people, a few of whom end up in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETHOS sits across 'get hospitalized'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the distinctive spirit or character of a community or culture.
